title: Drain finishes, close stops
text: After `drain()`, the executor rejects new injections but injects the events already queued, lets running actions finish and ends once quiet. `close()` rejects new injections too, but an event still queued when the executor takes the close is never injected, and the run ends as soon as no action is in flight.

steps.text: The place `order` is an environment place. One order is in the marking, a second is still queued, and the host calls `drain()`. A third `inject()` now returns `false`.
Draining changes nothing in the cycle: the action of `pack` finishes and `ship` fires.

The queued order is injected, as `drain()` promises. Had the host called `close()` instead, Java and TypeScript would drop this order and complete its `inject()` with `false`; in Rust and Python the close travels behind the events sent before it, so the order is still injected.
Nothing is armed, in flight or queued. The drained executor ends the run, emits `ExecutionCompleted` and reports why it stopped.
